audit_findings.title: Negative-anchor growth reverses the scenarios
audit_findings.magnitude: BULL operating and equity value are $642 million below BEAR, and BULL value per share is $1.41 below BEAR
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth is multiplied by negative anchor OE, so higher assumed growth enlarges losses through the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We are focused on driving sustainable long-term growth and profitability through increased demand for our core product categories, continued expansion of our direct-to-consumer capabilities and strategic development of our global wholesale network.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated modeling error. The scenario ordering is economically reversed, and perpetually capitalizing losses makes the reported DCF values unsuitable for an investment conclusion. A valid recovery model could produce higher or lower values, so the directional correction cannot be established from the current inputs.
audit_findings.action: Replace percentage growth on negative OE with explicit annual revenue, margin, reinvestment and recovery paths that produce monotonically improving BEAR, BASE and BULL outcomes; otherwise suppress all DCF values and retain only the too-hard conclusion.

audit_findings.title: FY2026 OE may retain interest on already-defeased debt
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 total interest expense was $52.9 million; restricted-investment income was $13.9 million; the $600 million notes carried a computed $19.5 million annual coupon; exact OE correction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: OE retains interest expense while purging portfolio interest income, even though the bridge is dated after the defeased notes and their restricted assets were settled.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense, which includes amortization of deferred financing costs, bank fees, capitalized interest for long term property and equipment projects and interest expense under the credit and other long-term debt facilities, including defeased debt, was $ 52.9 million for Fiscal 2026 (Fiscal 2025: $ 24.6 million; Fiscal 2024: $ 22.8 million).
audit_findings.explanation: The numerator-to-bridge mismatch is demonstrated, although the exact correction is unresolved because total interest expense combines the defeased notes, continuing debt, fees, amortization and capitalized interest. The $19.5 million annual coupon equals 18% of the absolute $108.3 million anchor, making the issue reasonably capable of materially changing normalized OE and its capitalized value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain a debt-level FY2026 interest schedule, match the defeased-note coupon, financing-cost amortization and restricted-investment income, neutralize those items consistently, and rerun using a full-year burden for only the $400 million 2030 notes, $200 million revolver and recurring fees.

audit_findings.title: A finite litigation payment may have been capitalized as a perpetual loss
audit_findings.magnitude: $98.5 million FY2026 accrual, including $90 million paid and $8.5 million accrued; the $98.5 million charge equals 91% of the absolute $108.3 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any litigation charge or payment retained in anchor OE is projected and terminally capitalized, while any surviving unpaid claim belongs in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: During Fiscal 2026, the Company recorded an accrual of $ 98.5 million in respect of these legal proceeding contingencies within accrued expenses on the Consolidated Balance Sheets, of which $ 90 million was paid during the same period.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a large case-specific charge and payment, but the supplied OE workpaper does not establish how they entered the anchor. Capitalizing the paid amount would understate value; removing the whole charge without reserving a surviving obligation would overstate value. The scale is sufficient to change normalized OE materially.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $98.5 million charge and $90 million payment through net income, operating cash flow and the OE adjustments; remove each nonrecurring effect exactly once, then verify the appeal status and deduct any surviving prejudgment-interest obligation in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Restructuring creates a two-sided normalization risk
audit_findings.magnitude: $171.507 million FY2026 charges, $40.606 million FY2026 cash payments, $44.331 million estimated remaining at March 31 and $38.680 million remaining at June 30
audit_findings.mechanism: Recorded restructuring costs can depress anchor OE, noncash charges may require add-backs, and unpaid or future cash restructuring obligations may require explicit forecast or bridge deductions.
audit_findings.evidence: The 2025 restructuring plan is now expected to be substantially complete by December 31, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The workpaper treatment is unresolved, but the filed FY2026 charge equals 158% of the absolute $108.3 million anchor. Removing finite costs could materially raise normalized OE, while ignoring the remaining cash program could overstate equity value. The two effects must be separated rather than netted by assumption.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every restructuring category between expense, noncash add-backs, cash payments, working-capital movements and the June bridge; rerun OE after excluding only nonrecurring operating effects and explicitly recognizing the remaining cash obligations without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Unrecognized-tax-benefit liability is absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $110.8 million filed liability, including $23.3 million of interest and penalties; computed maximum scale is $0.24 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: A cash settlement not already captured in recurring forecast taxes would reduce the equity bridge dollar for dollar.
audit_findings.evidence: As of March 31, 2026, the total liability for unrecognized tax benefits was approximately $ 110.8 million (March 31, 2025: $ 95.1 million) including $ 23.3 million for the accrual of interest and penalties (March 31, 2025: $ 22.1 million).
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted filed liability is demonstrated, but its valuation adjustment is not. The filing cannot reasonably estimate settlement timing or amount, and some benefits could affect other tax accounts rather than cash. The record therefore does not establish how much of the $110.8 million is incremental to forecast OE or whether the resulting deduction is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June tax-contingency roll-forward by jurisdiction, expected settlement amounts and timing, offsets and treatment in forecast cash taxes; then deduct or probability-weight only the incremental cash claim and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may have been treated as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $395.981 million added to the bridge; March foreign cash was $277.6 million, including $263.3 million indefinitely reinvested; the full bridge addition equals a computed $0.86 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Only cash distributable after operating-liquidity, seasonal working-capital, restriction and transfer requirements should be added as non-operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: As of March 31, 2026, approximately $277.6 million of our cash and cash equivalents was held by our foreign subsidiaries, of which approximately $263.3 million is indefinitely reinvested.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding the entire June cash balance is demonstrated, but the amount genuinely excess is unresolved. The foreign-cash disclosure alone does not prove that funds are trapped, and the filing says related incremental taxes are not expected to be material; nevertheless, the full cash addition equals about 16% of the $5.25 market price and is reasonably capable of changing a valuation threshold after the DCF is repaired.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a June entity-level cash schedule and a normalized seasonal liquidity analysis covering inventory builds, payables, covenants, restrictions, transfer costs and minimum operating cash; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably distributable excess cash.
